def var_cov_var_normal(P, c, mu=0, sigma=1):
    """
    Variance-covariance calculation of daily Value-at-Risk in a
    portfolio.

    Parameters
    ----------
    P : float
        Portfolio value.
    c : float
        Confidence level.
    mu : float, optional
        Mean.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Variance-covariance.
    """

    alpha = sp.stats.norm.ppf(1 - c, mu, sigma)

#!/usr/bin/env python
import sys

from setuptools import setup

import versioneer

DISTNAME = 'pyfolio'
DESCRIPTION = "pyfolio is a Python library for performance"
"and risk analysis of financial portfolios"
LONG_DESCRIPTION = """pyfolio is a Python library for performance and risk analysis of
financial portfolios developed by `Quantopian Inc`_. It works well with the
`Zipline`_ open source backtesting library.

At the core of pyfolio is a so-called tear sheet that consists of
various individual plots that provide a comprehensive performance
overview of a portfolio.

.. _Quantopian Inc: https://www.quantopian.com
.. _Zipline: http://zipline.io
"""
MAINTAINER = 'Quantopian Inc'
MAINTAINER_EMAIL = 'opensource@quantopian.com'
AUTHOR = 'Quantopian Inc'
AUTHOR_EMAIL = 'opensource@quantopian.com'
URL = "https://github.com/quantopian/pyfolio"
LICENSE = "Apache License, Version 2.0"

classifiers = ['Development Status :: 4 - Beta',
               'Programming Language :: Python',
               'Programming Language :: Python :: 2',
               'Programming Language :: Python :: 3',
               'Programming Language :: Python :: 2.7',
               'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.4',
               'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.5',
               'License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License',
               'Intended Audience :: Science/Research',
               'Topic :: Scientific/Engineering',
               'Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Mathematics',
               'Operating System :: OS Independent']

support_ipython_6 = (sys.version_info >= (3, 3))

install_reqs = [
    'ipython>=3.2.3' if support_ipython_6 else 'ipython>=3.2.3, <6',
    'matplotlib>=1.4.0',
    'numpy>=1.11.1',
    'pandas>=0.18.1',
    'pytz>=2014.10',
    'scipy>=0.14.0',
    'scikit-learn>=0.16.1',
    'seaborn>=0.7.1',
    'empyrical>=0.5.0',
]

test_reqs = ['nose>=1.3.7', 'nose-parameterized>=0.5.0', 'runipy>=0.1.3']

extras_reqs = {
    'test': test_reqs,
    'all': test_reqs
}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    setup(
        name=DISTNAME,
        cmdclass=versioneer.get_cmdclass(),
        version=versioneer.get_version(),
        maintainer=MAINTAINER,
        maintainer_email=MAINTAINER_EMAIL,
        description=DESCRIPTION,
        license=LICENSE,
        url=URL,
        long_description=LONG_DESCRIPTION,
        packages=['pyfolio', 'pyfolio.tests'],
        package_data={'pyfolio': ['data/*.*']},
        classifiers=classifiers,
        install_requires=install_reqs,
        extras_require=extras_reqs,
        tests_require=test_reqs,
        test_suite='nose.collector',
    )

    "dates = pd.date_range(start='2020-01-01', periods=n_days, freq='B')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Simulate returns with some drift and volatility\n",
    "mean_return = 0.001  # 0.1% daily\n",
    "volatility = 0.02    # 2% daily volatility\n",
    "returns = pd.Series(\n",
    "    np.random.normal(mean_return, volatility, n_days),\n",
    "    index=dates,\n",
    "    name='strategy_returns'\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Generated {len(returns)} daily returns\")\n",
    "print(f\"Mean return: {returns.mean():.6f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Std deviation: {returns.std():.6f}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Visualize the returns and cumulative performance"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "6",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 8))\n",
    "\n",
    "# Plot daily returns\n",

    "axes[0].axhline(y=0, color='r', linestyle='--', alpha=0.3)\n",
    "axes[0].set_ylabel('Return')\n",
    "axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Plot cumulative returns\n",
    "cum_returns = ep.cum_returns(returns)\n",
    "cum_returns.plot(ax=axes[1], title='Cumulative Returns', linewidth=2)\n",
    "axes[1].set_ylabel('Cumulative Return')\n",
    "axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Calculate Sharpe Ratio\n",
    "\n",
    "The Sharpe ratio measures risk-adjusted return. Higher is better.\n",
    "\n",
    "**Formula:** Sharpe Ratio = (Return - Risk Free Rate) / Volatility"
   ]

   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "8",
   "metadata": {},

    "sharpe = ep.sharpe_ratio(returns, risk_free=risk_free_rate)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Sharpe Ratio: {sharpe:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(\"\\nInterpretation:\")\n",
    "if sharpe > 2:\n",
    "    print(\"  Excellent risk-adjusted performance\")\n",
    "elif sharpe > 1:\n",
    "    print(\"  Good risk-adjusted performance\")\n",
    "elif sharpe > 0:\n",
    "    print(\"  Positive but modest risk-adjusted performance\")\n",
    "else:\n",
    "    print(\"  Poor risk-adjusted performance\")"
   ]

   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9",

   "source": [

   ]

   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,

    "running_max = np.maximum.accumulate(underwater)\n",
    "drawdown = (underwater - running_max) / running_max\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(12, 4))\n",
    "drawdown.plot(kind='area', color='red', alpha=0.3)\n",
    "plt.title('Underwater Plot (Drawdown)')\n",
    "plt.ylabel('Drawdown')\n",
    "plt.xlabel('Date')\n",
    "plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },

  },

   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "12",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [

    "sortino = ep.sortino_ratio(returns, required_return=required_return)\n",

    "print(f\"Sharpe Ratio:  {sharpe:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(\"\\nNote: Sortino ratio is often higher than Sharpe ratio because\")\n",
    "print(\"it only penalizes downside volatility, not upside volatility.\")"
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "13",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

    "The Calmar ratio is the annual return divided by maximum drawdown. Higher is better."

  },

   "source": [

    "annual_ret = ep.annual_return(returns)\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Calmar Ratio:     {calmar:.4f}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Annual Return:    {annual_ret:.2%}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Maximum Drawdown: {max_dd:.2%}\")\n",
    "print(\"\\nInterpretation:\")\n",
    "print(f\"  The strategy generates {calmar:.2f} units of annual return\")\n",
    "print(f\"  for each unit of maximum drawdown.\")"
   ]
  },

   "id": "15",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Summary of All Metrics"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "16",

   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Calculate all metrics\n",
    "metrics = {\n",
    "    'Annual Return': ep.annual_return(returns),\n",
